1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods — adjust downward by 1–3% for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.  
2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >30% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% for 1–3 days post-spike.  
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day average is below 34.00, forecast should not exceed 35.00; if above 36.00, cap at 37.00 to avoid overfitting.  
4. Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days forward for 15–30 day horizons to align with actual momentum.  
5. Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes — increase forecast by 2–5% when history shows <32.00 for 5+ consecutive days.  
6. Avoid forecasting above 36.50 unless confirmed by 3 consecutive days of upward momentum — cap at 36.50 for 30-day forecasts to prevent overconfidence.
